candidates.label: Factitial panniculitis (self-induced) due to repeated subcutaneous meperidine injections
missing_or_uncertain: Exact injection sites not documented; meperidine is not polarizable, so F12 does not exclude it

candidates.label: Sclerosing panniculitis (lipodermatosclerosis)
missing_or_uncertain: Typical lower extremity involvement absent; no venous insufficiency history

candidates.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
missing_or_uncertain: No peripheral eosinophilia; histology shows panniculitis not fasciitis

candidates.label: Morphea profunda
missing_or_uncertain: Typically no foreign-body giant cells; ANA normal

candidates.label: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
missing_or_uncertain: No atypical lymphocytes; benign histology; normal CBC and ESR

response.rationale: The history of self-administered subcutaneous meperidine for 3 years, combined with woody induration, ulceration, muscle contractures, and histopathology showing lobular panniculitis with fibrosis and foreign-body giant cells (without vasculitis or polarizable material), strongly supports factitial panniculitis from repeated injections. Other diagnoses are less consistent with the location, histology, and laboratory findings.
